subject: Accounting
title: Contribution Margin
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Contribution Margin.

hook.text: Each latte sells for $5 and costs $1.50 to make. That $3.50 leftover is the contribution margin.

buildup.text: Contribution margin = Price minus variable cost. It's what each sale contributes to covering fixed costs.

discovery.text: Once fixed costs are covered, every additional contribution margin dollar goes straight to profit.

twist.text: A product with thin margins needs massive volume. A product with fat margins can profit with fewer sales.

climax.text: Managers use contribution margin to decide pricing, product mix, and whether to drop weak products.

punchline.text: Margin per unit tells you if each sale is worth making.

quiz.question: What does contribution margin measure?
options: How much each sale contributes to covering fixed costs

details.summary: Contribution margin is the amount remaining from revenue after variable costs are subtracted. This topic explains how to calculate it per unit and as a ratio, and how managers use it for pricing, product-mix, and break-even decisions.
details.whyItMatters: Contribution margin reveals how much each product contributes toward covering fixed costs and generating profit. Without it, managers can't evaluate which products actually drive profitability.
takeaways: Contribution margin equals revenue minus variable costs for each unit sold
Products with higher contribution margins contribute more per unit to covering fixed costs
The contribution margin ratio shows what percentage of each sales dollar covers fixed costs and profit

faq.question: How do you calculate contribution margin?
faq.answer: Contribution margin per unit equals selling price minus variable cost per unit. The contribution margin ratio equals contribution margin divided by selling price. For example, a $50 product with $30 in variable costs has a $20 contribution margin and a 40% ratio.

faq.question: Why is contribution margin more useful than gross margin for decisions?
faq.answer: Contribution margin separates costs by behavior (fixed vs. variable), which directly supports short-term decisions like whether to accept a special order or drop a product line. Gross margin mixes fixed and variable production costs, obscuring this analysis.
